clue.text: Hoarding US money without interest, say

parts.note: a bill is an American banknote

indicators.note: 'say' tells us the next word is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: someone without interest is bored

explanation.surface: A remark that American cash earns no interest, perhaps from a disgruntled saver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' looks like stockpiling cash, but it is the British word for a large advertising board; 'say' marks the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board, the British word for an American billboard.

clue.text: Section of the orchestra making money

explanation.surface: An orchestral section that turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass are the trumpets, horns and trombones of an orchestra; brass is also British slang for cash.

clue.text: Say what's noticeable here in gifts generouSly Supplied?

indicators.note: 'Say' tells us to speak the phrase that describes the printed oddity

parts.note: in 'generouSly Supplied' the two S letters are printed as capitals: large esses

explanation.surface: A question about what stands out in a description of generous giving, with oddly capitalised letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S in 'generouSly' and 'Supplied' are 'large esses' (ess is the name of the letter S); 'Say' has us speak that phrase, which sounds like the answer. The capitals sit inside the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity shown in bestowing gifts, so its plural covers gifts lavishly handed out.

clue.text: Evil, heartless young man entering German city -a killer, naturally

indicators.note: 'entering' tells us one group of letters goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Bonn is a city in Germany, once the West German capital

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word evil is removed, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A villainous youth sneaks into a German city: a born murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle from 'Evil'; 'entering' splits the city after its first letter. The plant's name is Italian for 'beautiful lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade, the plant also called belladonna, is a poison found in nature.

clue.text: Cut short a game of cards

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A card game cut off before it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, so it means to cut short.

clue.text: Humiliates the lower classes, wanting financial resources

parts.note: in the British social grading scale A, B, C1, C2, D, E, the lowest classes are D and E
one's means are one's money and assets

explanation.surface: A snob belittling poor people who lack money.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades people A, B, C1, C2, D and E by occupation, so the lower classes are DE; 'wanting' is a link here, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade or lower their dignity, much as humiliating does.

clue.text: Subject to pressure, and one's beginning to crumble

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: 'beginning to' picks out the opening letter of the word crumble

explanation.surface: Something under pressure starts to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject under discussion.

clue.text: Duck given something to eat on lake

parts.note: tea in Britain is also an evening or afternoon meal
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck is fed at the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can mean a meal, not just the drink; 'on' puts L after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: See chaplain walk about

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a chaplain stroll around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here; 'about' gives RE, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the services' informal word for a military chaplain or priest.

clue.text: Had an affair, and didn't stop

explanation.surface: Someone who had a fling and kept it going.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on with someone is to have an affair; to carry on is also to continue.

clue.text: Several weeks in Capri — lovely!

indicators.note: 'in' signals that the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A holiday-maker raving about a few weeks spent on Capri.
explanation.definitionFit: A month such as the fourth of the year is a span of several weeks.

clue.text: Arrived back, having stupidly married dangerous robber

indicators.note: 'back' turns that short abbreviation the other way round

parts.note: ar. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives or arrived

indicators.note: 'stupidly' tells us the letters of married are muddled

explanation.surface: A newcomer who rashly married a violent thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes RA from AR; 'stupidly' rearranges MARRIED into MRAIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram-raider drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it, a violent form of theft.

clue.text: Female joined with boat builder going round American national park

parts.note: she refers to a female

indicators.note: 'going round' says the boat builder's name surrounds the joining word

parts.note: Noah built the ark in Genesis
and joins things together, meaning with

explanation.surface: A woman teams up with a shipwright touring a US park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the boat builder's name around the joining word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenandoah National Park lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia.

clue.text: House in Kent area, near motorway

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east (SE) of England
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Property details for a house in Kent close to the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, hence SE; the M1 motorway gives MI, with the digit read as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Become scared drunk will swallow freak concoction

indicators.note: 'will swallow' means the word for drunk takes another set of letters inside it

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of freak are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drunk downs a weird cocktail and gets frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' scrambles 'freak', and 'will swallow' puts that mix inside the slang word for drunk, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To take fright is to become alarmed or frightened.

clue.text: Having little money, I nicked a gold coin

parts.note: p for penny is the smallest British coin abbreviation
nicked is British slang for stolen

explanation.surface: Short of cash, someone confesses to pinching a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistole was an old Spanish gold coin.

clue.text: Brief scheme to secure temporary job?

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for scheme is lost

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
to cement something is to make it secure

explanation.surface: A short plan to land some temporary work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' docks the last letter of the scheme word. The question mark flags that a placement is one example of a temporary job.
explanation.definitionFit: A work placement is a fixed-term post, often for a student gaining experience.

clue.text: Spoke irritably when shot?

explanation.surface: Someone who answered sharply when photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to speak sharply; a snapped subject has been shot by a camera, photographed.

clue.text: Publicity campaign in support of our poet laureate

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: A publicity drive backing the national poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate when the puzzle appeared, so 'our' poet laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is an advertising push to sell a product.

clue.text: Poison initially tipped from dodgy canister

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, so the letters of canister are jumbled
'initially' takes the opening letter of the word tipped

explanation.surface: Poison first poured out of a suspect container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges CANISTER, and 'from' tells us the T ('initially tipped') comes out of it, leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notoriously deadly poison.

clue.text: Share out dice?

explanation.surface: Dividing up, or cutting into cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is a sharing out of spoils; to dice food is to cut it, which carving up also does.

clue.text: About middle of October he would have a party

indicators.note: 'About' says the contraction goes around that central letter

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he would

indicators.note: 'middle of' picks the central letter of the word October

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone planning a party around mid-October.
explanation.walkthrough: October has seven letters, so its middle is the fourth, an O; 'About' wraps the contraction around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively country-dance party.

clue.text: Yesterday's news troubled banshee

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of banshee are thrown about

explanation.surface: A distressed wailing spirit is old news.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone whose fame is past, an idiom for yesterday's news.

clue.text: Expression of surprise 500 years back?

indicators.note: 'back' tells us to read the whole of the joined pieces from the end

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Astonishment at something from five centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns D + AGE round to give the answer; the surface also hints at an old-fashioned exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, a mild oath.

clue.text: Travel in a city is a pain

indicators.note: 'in' says the travel word sits inside the city letters

parts.note: NY is New York
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Getting about in a big city is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a city' gives two pieces: A as written and New York's initials; 'in' puts the travel word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme pain.

clue.text: German writer cheers common people

parts.note: Günter Grass was a German novelist, author of The Tin Drum
to root for someone is to cheer them on

explanation.surface: A German author applauds ordinary folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots are the ordinary members of a party or movement.

clue.text: Checks up on European man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: vets means checks thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone checking on a European man's name.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' reads the checking word from bottom to top; 'on' places the European letter after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve is a common male first name, short for Stephen.

clue.text: Show contempt for part of barbecue?

explanation.surface: Scorn shown at a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting expresses scorn; a spit is a rod on which meat is roasted over a fire.

clue.text: Continental community with high hopes concerning place to live?

parts.note: EC is the European Community

indicators.note: high can mean drunk or off-kilter, so the letters of hopes are mixed

parts.note: re means concerning

explanation.surface: The European bloc full of optimism about where people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles 'hopes'; 'Continental community' is the old European Community, and 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosphere is the part of the world, or of space, where life can exist, a habitable zone.

clue.text: Fellow's talked of making appearance

indicators.note: 'talked of' says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a guy is a fellow; guy's is its possessive

explanation.surface: A man's reputation is said to make him show up.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or semblance.

clue.text: Go to street meeting

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: An instruction to head to a street gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting, usually between lovers.

clue.text: Sorrow making girl uneasy, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name; tense means uneasy

explanation.surface: A nervous girl's sadness, as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is regret for wrongdoing, a kind of sorrow.
